text:
sasha: quick canary update — after a leader shuffle we saw a bunch of immediate evict+refetch cycles for hot prefixes. i sketched a tiny "serial ticket" idea to make handoffs deterministic: stamp residency with Ticket(node_id, counter) + access_epoch; eviction orders by (access_epoch, ticket) with a short soft-pin on fresh transfers.

mike: ticket namespace question — node-local counter or global? and wrap safety?

sasha: node-local 64-bit counter + stable node_id. on restart node publishes a tombstone with last counter so others treat older counters as expired. practically no wrap risk, tombstone defends restarts.

anna: how do we avoid a stale ticket forever preventing eviction if the new owner never bumps it?

sasha: access_epoch (u64) bumped on access; eviction prefers higher epoch. ticket only tie-breaks. plus a configurable soft-pin window after transfer to avoid instant eviction.

jordan: transfer vs eviction race: what if source evicts while dest is pulling?

sasha: handshake: source sets TRANSFERRING + last_ticket, dest pulls, ACKs and adopts ticket, source clears on ACK. eviction defers if TRANSFERRING or hits a short timeout.

anna: background rehydrate concern — transient fills creating conflicting lower-priority residents?

sasha: rehydrates must request a ticket from the owner before promoting to resident; otherwise they stay transient and don't compete.

mike: rollout idea?

sasha: phased: (1) advertise ticket/epoch fields but leave old comparator, (2) collect telemetry for post-handoff refetchs, (3) opt-in per-shard flag, (4) flip default when stable.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: CI note — kv-cache/evict-ticket-sim flaky; recent run 2/3 seeds passed, investigate https://ci.internal/12345

sasha: thanks — i'll draft RFC + test plan (comparator unit tests, tombstone recovery tests, chaos failover w/ rehydrate + evict). will post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
